newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Enerco expects to meet forecast yr profit.
newsitem.headline: Enerco expects to meet forecast yr profit.

text.p: Gas utility Enerco NZ Ltd said on Wednesday it was comfortable with progress being made and believed it had the momentum to meet its full year forecast of an after tax profit of between $18.75 and $19.25 million.
Earlier, the company reported a first half net profit of NZ$12.89 million against $10.02 million in the corresponding period last year.
The company said continued success in signing up home gas customers, sound revenue growth and the containment of operating expenses was behind the 29 percent lift in profit.

"Given that we traditionally earn between 60 percent and 65 percent of our full year profit in the first six months, and barring unforeseen circumstances or unseasonal weather, we are well on track to achieve a full year profit within our forecast range," Enerco said.
The company said it had rapidly expanded its customer base and gas distribution network during the six months, particularly in Auckland.

More than 5,500 new home has customers have been connected (against 2,500 last year) and nearly 270 kilometres of new mains laid (100 km) and 60 km of existing mains rehabilitated (68 km). Total revenue grew by 14 percent in the six months, to $103.3 million. Gas revenue rose by nine percent and that from appliance sales, servicing and installation by 47 percent.

"Our strategy of expanding our business through home gas sales is seeing growth flowing into our financial results, with the revenue increase in this sector being close to 20 percent," the company said.
Revenue from business gas sales also increased seven percent on a large base.

Enerco said while the outlook for business gas sales remained strong, factors such as energy conservation, mergers and rationalisations were likely to slow down this growth rate in the current six months.
It had carefully managed the operating side of its business to ensure the costs associated with rapid expansion did not impinge on its ability to maintain profit growth.
On sales of more than $100 million, its earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) increased by 27 percent to $20.1 million. Provision for taxation was $7.3 million, up 19 percent.
The dividend re-investment scheme will remain suspended.
